title: We were wrong <num>{misses}</num> of <num>{total}</num> times. Here they are.
lede: We gave our band the worst input we could find, the on-chain exchange price on its own, across <num>{weekends}</num> weekends, and graded it against the first fresh price when the market came back. It missed <num>{misses}</num> times. Anyone can rebuild every row from the chain.
artAlt: A tall stack of sealed cards with one pulled out of line.

live.title: The live record
live.body: The band as the product runs it, fed by an around-the-clock source that answers every ten seconds. It is one weekend old: <num>{inside}</num> of <num>{total}</num> reopenings inside.
live.caption: Live record of weekend reopenings
live.note: This first weekend was graded after the fact, from our own minute-by-minute capture: the band at 23:59 UTC against the price published at 00:00. Later entries are sealed and timestamped before the market reopens, and marked as sealed.

stress.title: The stress test
stress.body: The same band, fed only a thirty-minute average of on-chain trades. At a weekend that price drifts away from the real one, because few people are trading. These are the <num>{misses}</num> times it left the band.
stress.captionMisses: Reopenings where the band was wrong
stress.captionAll: Every reopening in the stress test

baseline: For scale: doing nothing, and carrying Friday’s price through the weekend, was off by {median} at the median and as much as {max}, over {reopenings} reopenings. How to rebuild these tables.
